explanation: The pictures settled a debate: all four hooves leave the ground at once, but with the legs tucked under the body, unlike the stretched-out gallop painters had shown.

claims.text: In 1878 Eadweard Muybridge photographed a galloping horse in a rapid sequence of pictures.
Muybridge's 1878 sequence did not show a cheetah, a pigeon or a frog.
Muybridge's photographs showed that a galloping horse has all four hooves off the ground at one moment.
In Muybridge's photographs the moment with all four hooves off the ground comes with the legs gathered under the body, not stretched out as in many earlier paintings.
